description.en-US:
Review a web page without leaving Firefox. Click an element or select text, write a change request, and collect structured annotations across page navigation. Copy the result as Markdown or JSON for Pi, or send it directly through the optional local bridge.

The Pi bridge can queue one annotation or a whole review batch in the active Pi session and report queued, active, and completed states in the browser. After Firefox consent and a send action, the extension sends annotation content to Pi on 127.0.0.1. Pi may then send it to the model provider configured by the user. Saved annotations use Firefox extension storage. Page scripts cannot directly read that storage, but can inspect or alter notes rendered in the page. With permission and a running Pi bridge, page scripts can also trigger the on-page send controls without user activation. Permission checks do not establish per-job human approval. Avoid secrets. The extension is unavailable in private windows.

summary.en-US: Annotate webpage elements or text, send targeted change requests to Pi, or copy them as Markdown.

version.approval_notes: The Firefox package contains readable JavaScript generated from TypeScript, without bundling, minification, or remote code. The uploaded matching source ZIP includes SOURCE.md with Node.js 24, locked dependency installation, and reconstruction commands. The XPI includes LICENSE and THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md for the upstream MIT-licensed code. On first installation, it opens the bundled welcome.html page with usage and optional Pi setup instructions. The normal Pi workflow uses a send control after Firefox data-sharing consent. That permission is not per-job human approval: with permission and a running bridge, page scripts can trigger the page-DOM send controls without user activation. The background independently rechecks both optional data permissions before every send and job-status relay; denied or unavailable permission refuses the relay without prompting. Health carries no annotation text and remains permission-independent. These checks cannot retract requests already sent or authenticate other local HTTP clients. Content-script row and instance ownership fences late consent, send, poll and setup responses; synthetic fixtures cover overlap, invalidation and teardown/replacement. Retries remain explicit; accepted requests and admitted storage writes are not cancelled by teardown. The extension connects to Pi at http://127.0.0.1:17373; Pi may then send the content to the model provider configured by the user. The background also serializes local collection operations by verified sender origin. Schema v2 adds row/collection revisions and an ID counter; migration confirms v2 before emptying legacy v1 arrays. Failed loads/writes do not become empty collection saves. Isolated production-broker/two-page fixtures cover concurrency, migration, conflicts and recovery without real Pi or model traffic. The separate pi-extension/ directory is not included in the Firefox package. Firefox for Android is unsupported and excluded from this version's compatibility metadata. The extension is unavailable in private windows and stores annotations in Firefox extension storage. Page scripts cannot directly read that storage, but can inspect or alter rendered notes; this release does not redesign DOM isolation.

release_notes.en-US: Documentation-only maintenance: remove obsolete version-specific verification commands and stale source-candidate wording. Keep current security-backport checks, release instructions and privacy limits. Browser behavior, storage, permissions, bridge runtime and dependencies are unchanged.
